provenance.summary: Sign-in alone is self-serve, but reading or writing calendar events uses sensitive scopes, so real users need Google's verification: a verified domain, a privacy policy, a demo video, and a review Google says typically takes 3-5 business days, though some developers report weeks. Start verification early and launch to up to 100 test users meanwhile, knowing their tokens expire every 7 days.

accessLevels.name: Sign the user in with Google
accessLevels.mechanism: OAuth with basic profile scopes only; no Calendar access.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Agent estimate: project, consent screen, OAuth client, Composio auth config.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "If your app utilizes only non-sensitive scopes, it is not mandatory for your app to complete the app verification process."

accessLevels.recommendation: Self-serve. Basic profile scopes also keep long-lived refresh tokens while in Testing.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Testing-mode tokens don't expire after 7 days when "the only OAuth scopes requested are a subset of name, email address, and user profile."

accessLevels.name: Read the user's calendar events
accessLevels.mechanism: User OAuth token with a read-only Calendar scope.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Agent estimate: verified domain, privacy policy, scope justification and demo video, on top of setup.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete." Open-ended because developers report reviews stalled for 8+ weeks.

accessLevels.recommendation: Submit for verification as soon as the domain and privacy policy are live; launch to test users meanwhile.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Examples of sensitive scopes include reading events stored in Google Calendar"

accessLevels.name: Create and update events (e.g. fixtures)
accessLevels.mechanism: User OAuth token with a Calendar write scope. The narrowest options touch only calendars the user owns or the app created.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Agent estimate, same work as reading plus the write flow in the demo video.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Assumes write scopes are sensitive like read scopes. If Google classes the chosen scope as restricted, a paid security assessment adds weeks. Check the classification in the Console.

accessLevels.recommendation: Prefer calendar.app.created or calendar.events.owned over full calendar access, and read their classification in the Console before you build.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: calendar.app.created: "Make secondary Google calendars, and see, create, change, and delete events on them." Google's scope page doesn't state sensitivity.

prerequisites.description: A Google account and a Google Cloud project with the Calendar API enabled.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Composio: the Calendar API must be enabled in the Google Cloud project that owns your credentials.

prerequisites.description: A domain you own, verified in Google Search Console, that hosts your public home page.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console"

prerequisites.description: A public privacy policy on the same domain as the home page, describing how you use Google user data.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page"

prerequisites.description: A video showing how a user grants each requested scope and how the app uses the data.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Prepare a video that fully demonstrates how a user initiates and grants access to the requested scopes"

steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable the Calendar API
steps.detail: In the Google Cloud Console, create or pick a project, then enable the Google Calendar API in the API Library.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Composio's guide walks through the same steps for the Gmail API.

steps.title: Set up the Google Auth Platform (consent screen)
steps.detail: Enter app name, support email, audience (External for public apps) and developer contact. This name and logo are what users see instead of Composio's.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Wizard steps quoted from Composio's guide: App Information, Audience, Contact Information, Acknowledgement.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client with Composio's redirect URI
steps.detail: Create a Web application client and add Composio's callback as an authorized redirect URI. Copy the client ID and create a client secret.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Composio's guide gives https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add; newer Composio docs show v3 callback paths, so copy the one your auth config screen shows.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Calendar scopes
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the narrowest scope (e.g. calendar.app.created for fixtures) and add them under Data Access, where the Console shows which are sensitive or restricted.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: That the Console labels scope sensitivity is expected but not yet seen; to confirm in the hands-on run.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a GOOGLECALENDAR auth config that uses your own OAuth app, paste the client ID and secret, and pass the auth config to your sessions.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "To show your own app name and logo, create your own OAuth app and set a custom redirect URL."

steps.title: Add test users and test end to end
steps.detail: Keep the app in Testing, add yourself and early users (up to 100), and connect through Composio. Expect sensitive-scope refresh tokens to expire after 7 days.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Testing projects are "limited to up to 100 test users" (seen via search excerpt); Testing status "is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days".

steps.title: Prepare the verification pack
steps.detail: Home page and privacy policy on your domain, a justification per sensitive scope, and a demo video script showing consent and use.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope"

steps.title: Verify your domain in Search Console
steps.detail: Prove you own the domain listed as an authorized domain.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console"

steps.title: Publish the app and submit for verification
steps.detail: Move the app to In production and submit; record the demo video yourself. Until approved, users see the unverified-app screen and you are capped at 100 new users.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "your app will be limited to 100 new users until it is verified."

gates.name: Cloud project and OAuth client
gates.description: Create the project, consent screen and OAuth client to get a client ID and secret.

gates.name: Domain ownership
gates.description: Every authorized domain (home page, privacy policy, redirect domains you own) must be verified in Search Console.

gates.name: Brand verification
gates.description: Google checks the app name, logo, home page and privacy policy shown on the consent screen.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: No official figure found for brand verification on its own.

reviewerChecks.text: Home page is public and not behind a login.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users."

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "All apps that use Google APIs to request access to data must perform the following steps to complete brand verification"

gates.name: Sensitive scope verification
gates.description: Google reviews why you need each sensitive scope and how the app uses it before any Google account outside your test users can grant it.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete." Business days.

reviewerChecks.text: A justification for each sensitive scope.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope"

reviewerChecks.text: A demo video of a user granting the scopes and the app using them.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Prepare a video that fully demonstrates how a user initiates and grants access to the requested scopes"

reviewerChecks.text: A privacy policy on the same domain as the home page.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page"

rejectionReasons.fix: Reply on the verification email thread and keep scopes minimal; plan launch with test users meanwhile.

evidence.label: reported
evidence.note: Forum report of a sensitive-scope review under review for 8+ weeks (2026).

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "Sensitive scopes require review by Google before any Google Account can grant access."

fallbackWhilePending.text: Stay in Testing and add up to 100 test users; their sensitive-scope tokens expire after 7 days, so they reconnect weekly.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: Test user limit seen via search excerpt.

fallbackWhilePending.text: Keep using Composio's managed Google Calendar app until your own app is verified; users see Composio's name on the consent screen.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: The toolkit page lists Composio-managed OAuth as available.

fallbackWhilePending.text: Launch sign-in first: basic profile scopes need no verification.

whyGoCustom.text: Your own name and logo on Google's consent screen instead of Composio's.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "To show your own app name and logo, create your own OAuth app and set a custom redirect URL."

whyGoCustom.text: Scopes beyond what Composio's app is verified for: unverified extra scopes get the app blocked.

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: "The OAuth client is requesting scopes that Google hasn't verified for that client."

evidence.label: documented
evidence.note: From Composio's Google guide; newer docs show v3 callback paths. Copy the exact URI from your auth config screen.

openQuestions.question: Which Calendar write scopes does Google class as sensitive vs restricted? One vendor guide calls calendar.events restricted, which would add a paid security assessment.
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Restricted would move the write level from days of review to weeks plus a fee.

openQuestions.question: Is calendar.app.created treated as less sensitive than calendar.events?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: If so, a fixtures-only agent could pick the cheaper path.

openQuestions.question: Which redirect URI does Composio's GOOGLECALENDAR auth config show today (v1 auth-apps/add or a v3 callback)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: A mismatch breaks the OAuth flow with redirect_uri_mismatch.
